title: Yaman peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Yaman peanut: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Yaman peanut is a peanut variety from BPI NCRDC, Los Baños, Laguna. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Yaman is a registered peanut variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2001 as NSIC 2001 Pn 10. BPI NCRDC, Los Baños, Laguna bred it. It takes 89 to 92 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

items: **Days to harvest:** 89 to 92 days from sowing to harvest.
**Yield:** 1.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Yaman peanut takes 89 to 92 days from sowing to harvest. That is 10.7 days faster than the average of the 26 peanut varieties with a day count, 101.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.6 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.85. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against rust, cercospora leaf spot, so scout for them from the early weeks.

The pests and diseases that hit peanut fields most often: [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [eggplant leafhopper](/pests/eggplant-leafhopper), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 60 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed holds 30.2 percent crude protein.
Where and when to plant Yaman peanut

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Mani needs loose, well drained soil to fill its pods. Pick a variety by seed size for your buyer, and one rated against rust and leaf spot for the wet season.

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.

Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 89 to 92 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.6 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Yaman?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
